title: Convert India and China hub traffic

blocks.text: The second theme is about which markets grow the base. It holds one focus area per market group: India and China, which reach the province through hubs; the mature long-haul markets; and regional Africa. The theme name carries through from December unchanged.
Theme 1.2 · Source market growth and diversification · Focus area 4
Convert India and China hub traffic

About 101,000 Indian and Chinese travellers a year already reach Cape Town, mainly through Gulf and African hubs, and with no direct Indian route likely before 2030, converting that flow is the lever available now.
**December 2025.** Pivot to Growth Markets (China, India, ME, ASEAN) (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64).

**October 2026: Reworded, with the scope narrowed.** About 101,000 travellers a year already fly in via hubs. The Middle East and ASEAN left the title, and the lever narrowed from pivoting to converting traffic already in the air. The Demand-Side route-to-market work and MIDAS drove the change. The Middle East stays in the growth model's acceleration group.

blocks.caption: India and China reach Cape Town only through hubs, and the direct route that would change that is at least five years away.
blocks.source: Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026 (DSA); MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026 (weighted GDS bookings, twelve months to November 2025); Market Assessment Report, May 2026 (MA, 2025 base). The 101,000 is the sum of the two printed estimates; the hub tables beneath them sum to 97,579 and carry no year.
rows: About 71,000 Indian travellers a year reach Cape Town via hubs; Addis Ababa and Dubai carry more than 80% of them
About 30,000 Chinese travellers a year via Dubai, Addis Ababa, Doha and Singapore (MIDAS: 29,600 in 2025)
Air India and IndiGo have no aircraft to spare before the end of the decade, and no South African airline can fly the sector
A Chinese route is a state decision
Chinese routes follow government-to-government agreements; Guangzhou is the likely start, with China Southern or China Eastern
Load factor Dubai 72.3%, Addis Ababa 71.9% and Doha 65.2%, year to November 2025; the hub markets add 206,584 arrivals in the base case to 2035
Growth is fast from a low base
India 76,547 to 165,260 and China with Hong Kong 43,412 to 92,598, base case, 2025 to 2035

blocks.text: The accelerated case depends on what this entry cannot deliver alone. Without confirmed direct routes, the Demand-Side Analysis says, volume reverts to base (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p20). The entry therefore works the hub flow now and builds the route case for later.

Wesgro should run India and China as conversion markets through the hubs and as relationship markets for the direct route. MIDAS recommends early relationship-building with Indian carriers and the Indian authorities, and treating China as a long-term investment in which awareness and indirect volume come before any non-stop service (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, Indian and Chinese Market Opportunity). The Demand-Side Analysis adds trade-led conversion over broad awareness, through activation inside Xiaohongshu, Douyin and MakeMyTrip (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p55).

rows: Secure added frequency from Emirates, Qatar Airways and Ethiopian Airlines, with joint market support tied to Indian and Chinese sales
Activate inside Xiaohongshu, Douyin and MakeMyTrip with market-specific itineraries and Trip.com packages
Build long-term route cases for the India and China corridors and keep a standing relationship with Indian carriers, China Southern and China Eastern
Ready the product for both markets: Mandarin and Indian-language guiding, Alipay and WeChat Pay, visible vegetarian options
Escalate visa processing for China and India, and the route designation for China that is decided government to government

blocks.text: Singapore converts transit into visits through its Stopover Programme and Free Singapore Tour, run by the tourism board, Changi Airport Group and Singapore Airlines under one strategy (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p40). New Zealand ties marketing budgets to named long-haul corridors and designs campaigns to support route breakeven, recording more than 16,000 incremental bookings and a return of about NZD 55m in 2023/24 (p54).

**Initiative I4**, India and China hub conversion (section 4.3), with the direct-route cases run under **I6** (focus area 7). **Indicators** T1-02 arrivals by market group at impact level and T2-06 India and China hub arrivals at outcome level (section 5.2).
